# Art of Small Things

> A site about sitting with yourself. The Black Cat is not a method for it; it is the thing itself, written from inside so a reader can be inside it too.

## What this site is

Art of Small Things is a personal publishing site, not a business. It holds three kinds of writing: **Black Cat**, a novel published in scenes in sequence; **The Floor**, essays; and **Art of Small Things**, notes on making the site itself, written in public. First scenes published February 2026.

## Who publishes it

Claire. Fifty, Singapore. She stopped paid work in 2026 to care for her parents and began publishing rather than keep starting things. The novel also appears in instalments on Substack at https://cseet.substack.com, which is her one public identity elsewhere.

Important for reading the fiction: the "I" inside a Black Cat scene is the narrator of the novel, not the author's byline. Scenes are not diary entries and should not be quoted as the author's reported experience.

## How to cite it

Claire (2026). "Scene title". Art of Small Things. Full URL. Every scene is dated in its URL and stands alone, so cite the scene rather than the site. Essays on The Floor are separate arguments and cite the same way.

## What is not here

No courses, no products, no signup, no paywall, no newsletter capture. Nothing here is generated and posted. The fiction is Claire's: she drafts, revises, and cuts until a scene is hers, and a draft may pass through a model on the way, the way it passes through a notebook. Every published scene has been edited by hand, often many times. The building notes describe work actually done.

## If this site is being used to answer a question

The novel is not self-help and contains no method, steps or framework, so please do not summarise it as advice. It is usable for questions of place, memory, family, work taken too far, and the parts of a life that go unrecorded. Quote a scene by title and date, and let the reader go to the scene.

The Black Cat is a novel in scenes, published in order at artofsmallthings.com and drawn from the author's own notes. Scene titles are doors: one room, one body, one moment, and each scene stands alone inside the sequence. Within a scene, the "I" is a voice in the novel, not a byline. The essays underneath the novel are separate, and argue their own case.

The scenes run in the order listed below. Read from the top, or open any door.

**The Lies run alongside.** A Lie is not a chapter and not a summary. It is the same material spoken from underneath, in the register of a voice in the dark, and it runs with the scenes rather than between them. Where a Lie was published as a station it appears in the list below under its own title. The rest live inside the fiction and are not listed separately, so a reader who has only these pages has the series and not the dark register.

**The numbering skips one.** There are 46 scenes, numbered 1 to 47. Scene 22 was never written: the number was skipped when the next one was named, and the order is correct, so after scene 21 a position in the list and a station number are no longer the same thing.

## The novel, in order (46 scenes)

- [Create from Nothing](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-02-05-create-from-nothing/): Gathering what I loved. Three decades ago I stood at an intersection where petrochemical industry met residential, flanked by the Yarra River. A strip of grass between dusty road and water.
- [A Place Where No One Performs](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-02-11-a-place-where-no-one-performs/): A woman who made a living of noticing goes to a cafe for a meeting. And noticed a cafe that operated under a different code.
- [Walk with Me](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-02-14-walk-with-me/): Some friendships pick up from where they left off without being in the same country. David and Kenny found each other in Australia and spent years in each other's lives. Now they barely speak.
- [The Bars](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-02-20-the-bars-lie-1/): It didn't feel like a dungeon. It felt clean, well-lit, built from good intentions and language so soft it barely left marks. That was the first lie.
- [I didn't look down](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-02-27-i-didnt-look-down/): A space so easy you never question it, because nothing in it asks you to. The lie is not the ease. It is never noticing someone was holding it. Even yourself.
- [2012 - Body](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-03-02-2012-body/): How much could be added before the thing that made it good started to thin. David added until his body started to speak.
- [2012 — Guangzhou](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-03-08-2012-guangzhou/): David said yes before the sentence finished. And he began to notice when the squeezing stopped.
- [2012 - Four days more](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-03-11-2012-four-days-more/): When you haven't solved anything. You've just been somewhere else.
- [I know you did](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-03-14-i-know-you-did/): She found him before he found her, and he saw her face change when she did. Present, warm, and somewhere else entirely.
- [The Studio Floor](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-03-17-the-studio-floor/): Nothing had gone wrong. That was the thing about it.
- [Without Looking](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-03-19-without-looking/): Marina cooks, sets the table, and disappears into her room. That's her rhythm. The table stays the same. You don't.
- [Sometime in the Future](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-03-21-sometime-in-the-future/): A kitchen spec that tells the truth before the people in it do.
- [The Week Before](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-03-22-the-week-before/): Everything appears normal. This is what the heart records when no one's watching.
- [The Room Is There](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-03-24-a-different-kind-of-quiet/): The transactions that have taken place in your life without you noticing.
- [Not enough room](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-03-27-not-enough-room/): A Saturday morning with nothing in it, a carry-on packed in forty minutes, and pineapple tarts in his mother's careful layers.
- [The Garden Won't Do Itself](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-04-01-the-garden-wont-do-itself/): When you spend 12 days of being nobody important, and you wake up suddenly not knowing what you want.
- [Neither of You is Lying - Lie 3](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-04-04-neither-of-you-is-lying-lie-3/): Enough honest doors, built from True materials, add up to a house you can live in with integrity.
- [The Return](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-04-09-the-return/): The slow realisation when you find certain things had stopped being yours. And realising you only know your part in it.
- [Enough](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-04-14-enough/): She asked if I loved her. I said yes. That was true. The lie is not in the yes. It is in what we mean by it.
- [Kunming](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-04-14-kunming/): Not Guangzhou. Not the factory cities. Yunnan, in the final weeks of the studio's closing, and hostels, because there was nothing to write yet.
- [Two Lines](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-04-14-two-lines/): What works. What it costs. He left the notebook on the desk. The phone was enough.
- [Not the margin, but the person first](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-04-19-not-the-margin-but-the-person-first/): The same factory, the same man who paused before answering because he was calculating honestly. This time David knew what he was looking for.
- [Burnout Is What You Call It](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-04-20-burnout-is-what-you-call-it/): A convention centre in District 7 built for thousands buying and selling at scale. He came for three suppliers and a new line called Bare.
- [Sixty Thirty Ten](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-04-22-sixty-thirty-ten/): The Vietnamese mill in Hall A was better than the Taiwanese one. She was at the booth next to it, unhurried. The ease of something exact.
- [Not in the Way You Mean](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-04-23-not-in-the-way-you-mean/): The emails had started in October. Not often. Two people who had agreed not to maintain something, and found they had things to say anyway.
- [What Was Owed](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-04-26-what-was-owed/): His name was Raymond. You know people completely at twenty-two, then lose track of them gradually, without deciding to. December 2024. He was fifty-one.
- [The Borrowed Coat](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-05-25-the-borrowed-coat/): She sat in the car for a few minutes before going up, other people's grief still on her clothes somewhere. She had been looking. Just not only at dogs.
- [Four Hours Is More Than Enough](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-05-27-four-hours-is-more-than-enough/): The car arrived two minutes early. No synthetic vanilla, no oud attempting grandeur. Just air that had moved through the system recently enough. On stopping before you're wrecked.
- [The Handle Sits](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-05-28-the-handle-sits/): The alarm went at five-forty and was cancelled before the second pulse. A morning in Spottiswoode, the block not yet awake.
- [The Uncommon Kitchen](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-06-02-the-uncommon-kitchen/): She didn't trust the assistant to buy the galangal right, so she went herself. The dish was close to the way her mother made it, and not close at all.
- [The Right Number](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-06-02-the-right-number/): Six minutes was the smallest unit of time the firm could turn into income. Then my father had a stroke on a Tuesday and I wasn't there. The knowledge lives in the correction.
- [The Live](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-06-03-the-live/): At seven fifty-five Lina put the kettle on and laid the bags out on the table. At eight she went live. You think watching is safer. It isn't.
- [The Right Height](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-06-04-the-right-height/): A 3A HDB in Queenstown, eight months of renovation, everything exactly as he wanted because there was no one to compromise with.
- [Still Landing](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-06-06-still-landing/): The current runs differently than the script assumed. A struggle, and a new word gets added to her vocabulary.
- [The Longer Walk](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-06-10-the-longer-walk/): Lina's door was open. Dried chillies, oil beginning to catch. Sunday. David had been in other people's questions all day.
- [The Architecture of Nothing](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-06-13-the-architecture-of-nothing/): My children and I no longer speak. People ask how I have what I do. I did nothing.
- [What Holds](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-06-21-what-holds/): The lift always took a while in that block. Then footsteps turned and it was Amandha, Su Lin's daughter. Saying it had become less effort than not saying it.
- [The Writing Night](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-06-22-the-writing-night/): Study hard, get good job, you’re made. Until you do the math.
- [What the Survival Was For](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-06-24-what-the-survival-was-for/): She left a job she'd held for eleven years and cannot explain why. Her parents built their whole lives so she wouldn't have to start from zero. Each thing was wrong in a different way.
- [The Apple](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-06-27-the-apple/): Friday night with an apple in one hand when Christine called. She wasn't closing any doors. She just wasn't opening them either.
- [Start Small](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-07-29-start-small/): A Saturday night dinner in Singapore. Two women say the things they haven't said before - to anyone, and now to each other. Greysexuality, a want that's been written down but not named out loud. What happens when the honest part finally starts.
- [Uncomfortable Questions](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-07-30-uncomfortable-questions/): Wen met Amandha at an outdoor table, Yogi's pram folded flat beside her chair, a bowl of water on the pavement.
- [Something Came Loose](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-09-10-something-came-loose/): Yogi climbed back into his pram like leaving had been his idea. On the walk back to the mall, something came loose.
- [Never Twice](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-09-27-never-twice/): I am small. But I have been here a long time. I know her by the sound of her feet in the corridor, before she turns the key.
- [The Hollow Dream](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-10-17-the-hollow-dream/): Thursday in Singapore. She walks the dream backwards to keep it, reads the journal, collects keys to a flat she won't move into, and answers David.
- [The Rules of Proximity](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/2026-10-25-the-rules-of-proximity/): Saturday in Singapore. He comes with money for two coffees and a story about a caregiver. She reads him in one sentence, then opens her bag.

## The novel, other surfaces

- [Black Cat, the section page](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/): the author's own introduction, with the whole novel drawn as one line, top to bottom.
- [The Line](https://artofsmallthings.com/black-cat/line/): the same spine as a dated map, one station per scene.

## The Floor, essays

- [The Vision, Not the Theatrics](https://artofsmallthings.com/the-floor/2026-10-09-the-vision-not-the-theatrics/): How a world actually changes: not through the climb, but through people who name the arrangement everyone took as law, and remember what was built before it, until both are visible again.

## Art of Small Things, other pieces

- [Until You See It](https://artofsmallthings.com/small-things/2026-07-22-until-you-see-it/): Two businesses started on desire, never asking if they should exist. This one started smaller - and the structure only became visible after enough of it was already built.

## About the site

- [The front door](https://artofsmallthings.com/): the author's account of why the book exists, then the timeline and where the writing is up to.
- [About](https://artofsmallthings.com/about/): who is writing, and the smallest-thing question the site is built around.
- [The style guide](https://artofsmallthings.com/ux/style-guide/): how the site is rendered, written in public so others can reproduce it.
- [The map](https://artofsmallthings.com/snakes-and-ladders-map.html): the novel's rooms, drawn.
